analysis.summary: maxo makes Gorilla Tag videos about updates, mods, custom maps and crossovers. His thumbnails are clean 3D renders of a bright green gorilla with a red, white and blue headband, usually with no text and one small scene to read.
analysis.niche: Gorilla Tag updates, mods and custom maps

styleTraits.title: Green gorilla, striped headband
styleTraits.detail: Almost every thumbnail features his bright green gorilla with a red, white and blue sweatband, rendered in clean 3D with soft lighting rather than taken from raw gameplay. In the newest one, 'I Added Minecraft Into Gorilla Tag', he appears only as a green arm holding a diamond sword in first person.

styleTraits.title: Text is rare and short
styleTraits.detail: Only 8 of the 30 thumbnails in the sample carry a caption, always one or two words: 'NO MODS', 'banned', 'me', '0 Downloads', 'impossible.'. Most are thick white letters with a dark outline; 'banned' is red. 4 of the 5 most-viewed videos in the sample have no caption at all.

styleTraits.title: 'NO MODS' as a promise
styleTraits.detail: Three thumbnails print 'NO MODS' in huge white letters across the bottom. It answers the first doubt a Gorilla Tag viewer has about a wild clip: is this real or hacked? Results vary: about 591,000 views for 'Gorilla Tag Added Built-In MODS...', 256,000 for 'Gorilla Tag Added Custom Maps...' and 104,000 for 'Gorilla Tag Gave EVERYONE Mods...'.

styleTraits.title: 'me' and a red arrow
styleTraits.detail: When maxo is small in the frame, a lowercase white 'me' with a red curved arrow points him out: held in a giant robot's hand in 'Gorilla Tag Added TRANSFORMERS...', or as a camouflaged gorilla on a tree trunk in the Meccha Chameleon video.

styleTraits.title: A scene, not a pose
styleTraits.detail: The most-viewed thumbnails stage one moment with a rule you can read: maxo hiding in a lit hole in a wall while a police gorilla stands next to it, maxo flying up toward a floating tower under a giant banana, a huge maxo face beside a table of tiny gorillas building with blocks. Elsewhere a creature fills half the frame (SpongeBob, a purple tentacled alien, a giant robot) with maxo mid-size beside it.

standouts.why: 972,268 views, 6.8 times the 143,190 median, the biggest video in the sample. There is no text: maxo's green gorilla, in a yellow prison-style shirt, hides in a glowing white-outlined hole in a concrete wall with a finger to his lips, while a blue gorilla in a police cap and 'POLICE' shirt holds a toy gun right beside him. The game's rule, hide from the cop, reads in one look, and the near miss adds tension. It is a collaboration listed on several channels, which may also have widened its reach.

About 591,000 views, 4.1 times the median. A green and a red gorilla stand on a cliff edge, with 'NO MODS' in huge white letters across the bottom. The title says the game added mods; the thumbnail says 'NO MODS'. That apparent contradiction may create curiosity: mod-like powers without installing anything.

About 490,000 views, 3.4 times the median, two weeks after upload. A Minecraft hotbar, hearts and a diamond sword in a green first-person hand sit next to a purple gorilla in a top hat holding Minecraft items. The Minecraft interface says 'crossover' at a glance, even to people who don't play Gorilla Tag. It came after a three-month gap and five videos between 25,000 and 44,000 views, so pent-up interest may also play a part.

lessons: Give your avatar one fixed accessory (maxo's striped headband) so it's recognisable even when small.
Stage one moment with a readable rule, like hiding from a cop, instead of a posed character.
Use a short phrase only when it answers the viewer's main doubt, like 'NO MODS'.
Borrow a famous game's interface (the Minecraft hotbar and hearts) to say 'crossover' in one glance.
When you are small in the frame, label yourself with 'me' and an arrow.
analysis.experiment: Pick a video with a clear game rule (hide, chase, escape). Version A: your avatar posed in the setting. Version B: the same setting staged as one tense moment, such as your avatar hiding while the chaser stands next to it. Use no text on either. Compare them in YouTube's Test & Compare on watch time share.

faq.q: How many subscribers does maxo have?
faq.a: As of 23 October 2026, maxo has about 457K subscribers (YouTube's rounded figure) and around 270 videos. Across the 30 recent long videos in our sample, the median was 143,190 views. The biggest, 'EXTREME Cops VS Robbers in Gorilla Tag...', had 972,268 views.

faq.q: What does maxo make videos about?
faq.a: Gorilla Tag: new updates and live events, mods, custom maps, game modes like Cops vs Robbers, and crossovers such as 'I Added Minecraft Into Gorilla Tag'. Most videos (26 of the 30 sampled) run 8 to 15 minutes. Uploads have been irregular lately, with about three months between the Minecraft video and the one before it.

faq.q: What do maxo's thumbnails look like?
faq.a: Clean 3D renders of his bright green gorilla with a red, white and blue headband, often in a small staged scene or next to a large creature or character. Most have no text: only 8 of the 30 we sampled carry a caption, such as 'NO MODS', 'banned' or 'me' with a red arrow.

Gorilla Tag, the VR game where players move as gorillas using their arms. Every video in our sample is about it, though some bring in other worlds through custom maps, such as SpongeBob's Bikini Bottom, Lethal Company or Minecraft.
